title: Broker Non-Payment Bond-Claim Collective for Small Carriers
one_liner: A service that files carriers' unpaid-load claims against the broker's surety bond and FMCSA record, pools every claimant against the same broker, and publishes a real days-to-pay broker score built from actual payment outcomes.
customer: Small carriers and owner-operators (1 to 10 trucks), including hot-shot and box-truck carriers who don't factor every load. A second revenue stream comes from carriers who pay to check brokers before hauling.
problem: Small unpaid loads are too small for a lawyer and too big to shrug off. One carrier reported a $600 CAD load completed in November 2025 still unpaid in June 2026, after 50+ emails and calls that got only automated replies from a 'Legal Dispute Department'. Their workaround was to 'sign up with factoring companies' who 'either approve or deny'. Meanwhile freight rates have stayed squeezed since 2022, so broker failures and slow payers keep coming.
solution: The carrier uploads the rate confirmation, proof of delivery and invoice. The service verifies the broker's authority and bond or trust-fund status from public FMCSA data, sends a formal demand, and files the claim with the broker's surety (federal rules require property brokers to carry financial security, at $75,000, which is paid out pro rata when many claimants exist). It files an FMCSA complaint and logs every step. The key mechanic is pooling: claims against the same broker are grouped so its claimants are first in line and can cite a pattern. All outcomes feed a broker pay-speed database ('median days to pay', 'claims filed', 'claims paid') that carriers check before booking a load. A trucking attorney reviews templates to stay clear of unauthorized-practice issues.
why_now: The freight recession is still going: the owner-operator thread 'Rates are crashing and fuel to the moon!' began in March 2022 and was on page 1,134 as of Sept 26, 2026. Squeezed brokers pay slowly or fail, and forums are full of fraud and non-payer alerts. Document-heavy claim filing can now be automated cheaply. Factoring companies increasingly reject unknown or slow brokers, which pushes more risk back to unfactored small carriers.
revenue_model: 20 to 25% contingency on recovered amounts. A $15 per month subscription for broker pay-speed lookups and alerts. Later, sell the broker payment-behavior data to factoring companies and load boards.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not the collection letter but the payment-behavior data no credit bureau has, and it is created only by filing claims in bulk. The owner of one 'fraud alert' thread described 50+ emails and only automated replies over 7 months for a $600 CAD load, with a second victim in the same thread and factoring as the only workaround (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13536421/). The margin squeeze is ongoing: the rates-and-fuel thread reached page 1,134 in Sept 2026 (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13542683/). A new-authority owner-operator says he cannot get financing and rents a box truck by the day, missing about $4,000 a day in loads, which shows how thin small carriers' cash is (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13465676/). The bond rule detail is from general knowledge of FMCSA broker financial-security requirements and needs legal confirmation.
first_30_days: Week 1: recruit a trucking attorney to review one claim template. Post in the TruckersReport Freight Broker forum offering free claim filing to carriers in the fraud-alert threads. Weeks 2 to 3: file 15 to 20 claims by hand, group them by broker, and record response times. Week 4: publish the first 'days-to-pay' leaderboard of 25 brokers, and start charging 20% contingency. Target: 30 claims filed and 5 paid, with the leaderboard as the top-of-funnel.

title: Paper-Mill Shield for Diamond Open-Access Journals
one_liner: An Open Journal Systems plugin and service that screens incoming manuscripts and reviewers using public research detectors, and hands volunteer editors a plain-language decision memo.
customer: Library-publishing programs, university presses, national journal platforms and scholarly societies that run dozens to thousands of small journals on Open Journal Systems (OJS). The buyer is the consortium or library publishing unit, not the individual journal, whose budget is close to zero.
problem: Paper mills, LLM-generated manuscripts and fake reviewer identities hit small journals run by volunteer editors. Big publishers have enterprise integrity suites (Clear Skies, the STM Integrity Hub). Small journals have nothing, and a single wave of fraudulent papers can get them delisted from Scopus or Web of Science.
solution: Submission-time screening chained from public sources: Problematic Paper Screener fingerprints (tortured phrases, ChatGPT tells), reference-list checks against the Retraction Watch database now openly available through Crossref, citation-cartel and author-network anomalies via OpenAlex, and reviewer-suggestion checks (ORCID, email domain and institution mismatches). Flagged items go to a human integrity analyst. The editor receives a one-page memo with evidence and a suggested action, not a score. Includes a backlist audit product.
why_now: Paper-mill scale is now documented (the Problematic Paper Screener scans on the order of 130M publications weekly and has fed 1,000+ retractions). Retraction Watch data went open via Crossref. LLM text makes fakes cheap. Diamond open access is growing fast because of funder mandates, which means more volunteer-run journals with no integrity budget.
revenue_model: USD 3-10 per screened submission for individual journals. Consortium plans at USD 2-15k per year covering a platform's journals. Fixed-fee backlist audits per journal. Human analyst escalations billed hourly.
non_obvious_insight: The detectors already exist as free tools used by sleuths. What editors lack is accountability packaging: a defensible written memo they can cite when rejecting an author, and someone to escalate to. Sell decision memos to the consortium that hosts the journals, not detection scores to journals.
first_30_days: Build the pipeline as a command-line tool first, then an OJS plugin. Approach three library publishing programs and the PKP community forum. Offer 5 free backlist audits to journals that consent to anonymized findings. Publish a 'state of small-journal fraud' write-up from the audits as the PR hook. Sign one consortium pilot at a nominal fee.

title: Extranet Takeover Defense for Independent Hotels
one_liner: Managed monitoring and fraud response for hotels' OTA extranet logins and guest-messaging channels, the credential theft that turns into guest payment scams.
customer: Independent hotels, B&Bs and small STR managers of 10-150 rooms, their channel-manager and PMS resellers, and cyber insurers.
problem: Attackers phish or infect front-desk staff, take over OTA extranet accounts and message arriving guests from the genuine booking thread asking for payment via fraudulent links. The hotel absorbs chargebacks and reputational damage and can lose OTA account standing. These hotels have no IT staff and are too small for security vendors.
solution: A light service that watches for leaked credentials tied to the hotel's domain and staff emails, alerts on suspicious extranet login emails, flags guest messages containing external links or payment requests, and runs 10-minute staff phishing training. It adds a 24/7 hotline for incident response and a guest-facing 'how we ask for payment' page.
why_now: AI-written phishing in dozens of languages, widely reported hospitality-targeted credential theft campaigns in 2025, and merchant-model payments that concentrate risk in OTA accounts. Insurers are hardening cyber requirements.
revenue_model: EUR 49-149 per property per month, insurer commissions and per-incident response fees.
non_obvious_insight: The weak node is the hotel's front-desk laptop, not the OTA platform. The unit of attack is a booking thread the guest already trusts, so simple detection at the message level gives most of the protection.
first_30_days: Run a free credential-exposure scan for 100 hotel domains using public breach data. Send each hotel its results, convert 10 to paid, and partner with two hotel associations for distribution.

title: Pay Farmers to Under-Irrigate, Not Fallow
one_liner: A broker and satellite-verification layer that pays growers of alfalfa, hay and cotton for mid-season deficit irrigation and hands corporate and municipal buyers audited acre-feet.
customer: Buyers: corporate water coalitions (Amazon put $20M into the Water Resilience Coalition's Colorado River effort, $32M raised toward a $100M goal) and Lower Basin cities and water agencies. Sellers: irrigation districts and forage/annual-crop growers. The buyer pays.
problem: The 2027-2036 Colorado River framework pushes cuts onto agriculture (about 70% of the river), yet corporate money has no settlement layer. Fallowing is politically toxic and guts farm income. Drip and efficiency upgrades often do not reduce consumptive use, so nobody can say what a verified acre-foot is.
solution: A standard split-season contract. The grower skips the last irrigation cycles, or accepts deficit irrigation at pre-agreed growth stages. Consumptive use is measured by satellite ET (an OpenET-style ensemble) against a five-year baseline and paired control fields. Payment is escrowed per verified acre-foot, and the buyer gets a basin-and-year-tagged certificate. Wedge product: one district pilot plus a buyer dashboard. Federal credit is not needed to start, so begin with districts that already hold Reclamation conservation agreements.
why_now: The Aug 2026 Record of Decision fixed the 2027-2036 rules. Powell plus Mead storage is about 36% of capacity, the lowest since before Glen Canyon Dam filled. Corporate money is arriving, and open ET datasets are now good enough to audit individual fields.
revenue_model: 10-15% spread on each acre-foot transaction (roughly $40-90 on a $400-600/af price), plus $20-50k/yr verification SaaS to districts.
non_obvious_insight: Only cuts in consumptive use create basin-level savings, and forage crops tolerate a mid-season deficit far better than farm economies tolerate fallowed fields. Buyers are really paying for measurement certainty, so whoever owns the audit trail sets the price and the standard.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: run retrospective ET for 10 alfalfa/hay growers in one Lower Basin or Grand Valley district (public data, free tier) and price the acre-feet they could offer. Days 10-25: build a one-page buyer pitch and dashboard mock. Days 25-30: pitch the Water Resilience Coalition and two city water agencies to underwrite a 500-1,000 af pilot for the 2027 season, since contracts get negotiated over winter.

title: Blue UAS Bill-of-Materials Origin Auditor
one_liner: Part-by-part origin verification so 60,000-drone orders do not fail on hidden Chinese-origin motors, radios and cameras.
customer: Drone makers and their integrators selling to DoD and public safety, and the primes that must certify their subcontractors' parts.
problem: Compliance requires proving that components meet domestic-content and ownership rules, but sub-tier motors, ESCs, batteries and cameras often trace to opaque distributors. Manufacturers self-certify with spreadsheets and hope a re-labelled part is not found mid-contract.
solution: Upload a BOM and receive origin confidence per part. Cross-check import records, distributor invoices, factory databases and optional lab teardown or spectrum fingerprinting of sample units. Deliver an auditor-ready dossier and alerts when a supplier changes source.
why_now: Drone Dominance orders make component provenance a gating item for tens of thousands of units. About 48 defense firms are IPO candidates and want clean compliance records. Gauntlet winners must scale quickly and can't afford a failed audit (verify statutory citations).
revenue_model: $5-25K per BOM audit, $2-8K per month for monitoring, and per-sample teardown fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not certification but suppliers' unofficial data. Trade-data analytics plus teardown labs beat legal-only compliance firms because they can catch a repackaged part.
first_30_days: Audit 3 drone BOMs for free to build a dataset. Hire a customs-data analyst and a contract RF engineer. Pitch Gauntlet participants directly.

title: Bonded Escorts for Sedated Outpatient Patients
one_liner: A background-checked adult who legally receives your discharge instructions and takes you home after a colonoscopy or other sedated procedure, sold to the clinics that lose the slot when you have no ride.
customer: Independent GI groups and ambulatory surgery centers pay $65-95 per escorted visit. Solo agers and estranged or far-from-family adults pay $99-149 directly as a fallback.
problem: Most sedation centers will not proceed unless a responsible adult picks the patient up and hears the discharge instructions, and many refuse to release a sedated patient to a rideshare driver. Patients with no spouse, no nearby family, or no friend willing to sit through the aftermath of a bowel prep cancel, delay screening, or no-show. The clinic eats an empty high-margin slot. The patient feels embarrassed to ask and avoids the procedure.
solution: A regional network of vetted, insured escorts drawn from CNAs, retired nurses, EMTs and nursing students. The clinic scheduler adds one line to the booking call: 'No escort? Tap here and we will send one.' The escort meets the patient at the door, is named on the chart as the responsible adult, receives instructions, rides home with the patient, stays 20-30 minutes until the patient is settled, and texts a family contact. A clinic dashboard shows escort confirmed, so day-of cancellations for this reason disappear. Later add the required 24-hour post-anesthesia overnight companion, then cataract, oral surgery, and cosmetic and orthopedic day surgery.
why_now: The USPSTF lowered the colorectal screening start age to 45, which added millions of eligible patients. Procedures keep migrating to ambulatory surgery centers, which run on tight slot economics. The share of older adults living alone (solo agers) is at a record high. Checkr-style vetting and Stripe Connect-style payouts let a tiny team stand up a bonded, insured gig network in weeks. No incumbent sells 'the adult on the chart' to schedulers.
revenue_model: Per-visit fee paid by the clinic ($65-95, escort keeps about 60%) or patient-pay ($99-149). Add-ons include overnight post-anesthesia sitters billed hourly. Later, Medicare Advantage plans buy escort-with-transport as a supplemental benefit.
non_obvious_insight: The escort rule is a liability policy, not a medical one, so what the clinic needs is a credentialed name on the chart that satisfies the discharge nurse, not a ride. Nobody sells to the scheduling desk, where the cancellation leak is measured in dollars per slot. The patient's real barrier is shame at asking a friend to witness a colonoscopy, which a professional stranger removes.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 15 escorts from nursing-school boards and retired-nurse groups. Get a general and professional liability quote and run Checkr checks. Visit 10 GI practices and offer a free 30-day pilot where they pay only when an escort saves a slot that would have cancelled. Launch a landing page and a Twilio text line, and buy Google Ads on searches like 'colonoscopy no one to drive me home'. Run dispatch from a spreadsheet. Goal: 40 escorted procedures and 3 signed clinics.

title: Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers
one_liner: A verified job-placement and completion ledger that makes short-term training programs (CDL, CNA, welding, HVAC, medical assistant, cosmetology) audit-ready for the governor and Secretary approvals that Workforce Pell requires.
customer: Small proprietary career schools, community college workforce and continuing-education units, and employer-training nonprofits running 8-15 week programs. The program owner or director pays. State workforce boards are a second buyer because they were given no new resources to verify placement.
problem: The Workforce Pell final rule (published May 19, 2026; effective July 20, 2026, with early implementation from July 1) covers programs of 150-599 clock hours and 8-15 weeks. A program must show 70% completion and 70% job placement, measured over the 12 months before it applies and annually after that. The governor must first certify the program as high-skill, high-wage or in-demand, then the Secretary approves. Providers must submit completer lists and the information needed to verify placement. Commenters flagged burden for small providers and noted states got no new resources to run the framework. Separately, the earnings-premium rule (effective July 1, 2027) strips Direct Loan access from programs that fail in two of three consecutive years. The Department estimated 93% of cosmetology programs would fail under the proposal.
solution: At completion the system automatically sends completers and employers text and email verification requests at 30, 90 and 180 days. It collects pay stubs, employer confirmations and consent for state wage-record matching, and reconciles them to the rule's placement definition. It produces the governor's application packet (completer list, placement evidence, tuition versus earnings benchmarks) and the annual recertification. It also scores each existing program's exposure to the earnings-premium test using public program-level earnings data so owners can decide what to keep, fix or convert into a short-term program.
why_now: The 12-month look-back means a provider that is not tracking verified placement now cannot apply in 2027. The earnings-premium test takes effect July 1, 2027 and is already being scored on 2021 completers' 2025 earnings. States are building governor-approval processes this fall, and Workforce Pell went live July 2026.
revenue_model: $4-12k per year per program subscription, or $150-300 per completer verified. $3-5k fixed fee for the governor application packet. Earnings-premium exposure report for $1.5-3k. Later, licensing to state workforce boards for verification.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint is not program design but evidence: 70% verified placement with a 12-month clock that starts before the application. Short-course providers such as CDL, CNA and barbering schools typically track completion, not verified employment, so most will discover the gap after the clock has started. The final rule requires providers to give the Governor 'necessary information to verify the job placement rate', and it aggregates small programs' completers up to four award years to reach a 30-student minimum, which favors providers with clean historical records. The Title IV survival angle (93% of cosmetology programs were projected to fail the earnings test under the proposal) gives the same customer a second, more urgent reason to buy. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/19/2026-10013/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand-driven-workforce-pell-pell-grant and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/01/2026-13286/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand--driven-workforce-pell-student-tuition
first_30_days: Pick two states whose governors have opened a Workforce Pell approval process. Recruit five schools in different fields, including one at-risk cosmetology school, with a $1.5k pilot price. Backfill the last 12 months of completers by text and employer email to produce a baseline verified placement rate. Deliver a sample governor packet and an earnings-premium exposure score for each. Use the results to pitch the state workforce board on verification capacity.

title: Powered Public Land Brokerage for Robotaxi Depots
one_liner: A broker that matches autonomous-fleet operators to cities' already-energized, under-used land such as transit depots, fleet yards and city garages, on leases that trade concessions cities value.
customer: Robotaxi, autonomous delivery-van and driverless-truck operators pay success fees and retainers (Waymo, Zoox, May Mobility, Avride, Gatik and others). Cities and transit agencies are the counterparty, earning lease income.
problem: Depot power is the choke point for scaling robotaxis. A standard California charging site takes about 6 months, a new circuit 1.9 years, a substation upgrade 2.8 years and a new substation 8.9 years, and depots now compete with data centers for powered industrial land. Waymo's first 86M miles were only 54% passenger-carrying, so depots and reset cycles matter more than vehicles. AV operators do not know which public parcels are already energized, because they sit in transit-agency asset registers rather than commercial real estate databases.
solution: Build a dataset of municipally owned parcels with existing high-capacity service: bus depots, municipal fleet yards, park-and-ride lots, closed school-bus yards, airport lots and city garages. Overlay it with utility load-capacity maps. Use a template 'public benefit lease' (revenue share, 24/7 emergency access, data sharing, wheelchair-accessible service commitments, local cleaning and charging jobs) so cities can say yes without a full RFP. Then broker the deals.
why_now: Waymo raised $16B at a $126B valuation in Feb 2026 and is expanding across 10-14 metros. Zoox began charging fares on Aug 10, 2026, Tesla is running unsupervised in two states, and Aurora is exiting 2026 with 200 driverless trucks that need terminals. Large-load grid queues are freezing in Texas, so already-energized land is worth years.
revenue_model: A success fee of 3-5% of lease value or $75-150k per signed site, plus $10-20k/month retainers from fleets that want a standing pipeline. Optional revenue share with the city.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest input for autonomous-fleet scale is already-energized land, not compute or vehicles, and the largest holder of it is city government. City government cannot run a competitive marketplace but values non-cash concessions (accessibility, data, jobs) that a private landlord never offers.
first_30_days: In Texas, Arizona and Georgia metros with announced AV expansions, file public-records requests for depot and yard inventories plus utility service sizes. Build a 100-parcel shortlist. Pitch three fleet real-estate leads a paid $25k 'top-10 sites' report.

title: Human-Review Receipts for the EU Text Exemption
one_liner: Sell signed proof that a named human reviewed and took responsibility for AI-assisted text, which is the thing the EU's disclosure rule for text appears to reward, not labels on AI.
customer: Newsletter operators, niche and local publishers, and B2B content agencies that publish AI-assisted text to EU readers. Second buyers are legal and compliance leads at mid-market publishers.
problem: The industry reads EU AI Act Art. 50 (applicable Aug 2, 2026) as 'label the AI.' My understanding of Art. 50(4) is that the text-disclosure duty for public-interest publications has an exemption where content underwent human review or editorial control and a person holds editorial responsibility. Confirm the exact wording with counsel, because the brief does not quote it. Meanwhile readers get accusation tools: Substack embedded Pangram scanning on Jul 22 and LinkedIn added a slop-report button on Jul 30. Publishers have no defensible record of human review.
solution: A Ghost, WordPress and Substack-compatible plugin plus API that records, per article, the AI draft versus the final diff, who reviewed it, and a passkey-signed approval bound to the content hash. It publishes a verification page and a byline element ('reviewed and edited by [name]'), and generates an evidence binder for regulators and clients. If no review is recorded, it falls back to an automatic disclosure line.
why_now: Art. 50 became applicable on Aug 2, 2026, and reader-side detection has just been built into major platforms. The first regulatory questions and client audits will land on publishers this year.
revenue_model: $29-99/month per publication, $500-2,000/month agency plans, and $250 per audit-ready evidence binder.
non_obvious_insight: Detection tries to prove a negative ('not AI'). The law's structure turns human review into a legal safe harbor, so the sellable product is a positive: a named person accepted responsibility. That gives 'human-made' a compliance budget instead of an ethics budget.
first_30_days: Ship a Ghost/WordPress plugin with diff capture and passkey sign-off in about three weeks. Approach 10 EU-facing newsletters and 3 agencies with 'Aug 2 has passed, where is your evidence?' Co-brand the evidence binder with one EU tech-law boutique that can use it as a channel.

title: Resolution-Risk Ratings for Prediction Market Contracts
one_liner: A credit-rating-style score for how likely an event contract is to resolve ambiguously or be disputed, plus the rulebook basis between 'identical' contracts on different venues.
customer: Prop desks, market makers and arbitrage funds trading Kalshi, Polymarket and newer venues, at $300 to $3,000 per month. Venues and market creators pay for pre-listing rule linting.
problem: Polymarket logged more than 1,150 disputed markets in the first half of 2026, more than all of 2025. A US-Iran peace-deal market with over $345M in volume split traders on whether the outcome met a 'permanent' deal. Cross-venue arbitrage is not risk-free because sources, cutoffs and definitions differ, and displayed depth can vanish. Everyone prices the event, but nobody prices the contract wording.
solution: Parse each contract's rules (source of truth, timestamp cutoff, key definitions) and compare against a labeled history of disputes and oracle overrides. Output a 0-100 Resolution Risk Score with an expected haircut in cents. Give matched cross-venue pairs a scenario table of where they would settle differently, so arbitrageurs size positions correctly. Offer a 'rule linter' that flags ambiguous phrases for market creators, and deliver everything through an API and Discord/Telegram alerts.
why_now: Prediction-market volume is exploding (Kalshi reportedly passed $100B) and dispute counts are rising sharply. Institutional market makers are arriving and need risk inputs beyond price. Regulators and states are still fighting over these contracts, so rulebook and venue risk is priced by no one.
revenue_model: Desk subscriptions, per-market audit or lint fees from venues and market creators, and a data license to aggregators and terminals.
non_obvious_insight: Credit derivatives already lived through this. The asset's definition, meaning restructuring clauses and Determinations Committee rulings, became a priced factor, and an entire professional infrastructure grew around it. Prediction markets are at the 2003 CDS stage: the basis between 'identical' instruments is definitional risk. The winner is the rating-agency-plus-dispute-committee layer, not another odds aggregator.
first_30_days: Scrape resolved and disputed markets and hand-label about 300 disputes into an ambiguity taxonomy. Publish a public weekly 'Dispute Watch' with two or three calls that prove right. Sell to five arbitrage-bot shops through their Discord and Telegram communities at $500 per month. Offer free linting to prolific market creators for testimonials.

title: Fill-Level Sensors for Remote Vault Toilets
one_liner: Satellite-capable fill-level and usage sensors for the vault toilets on public land and in campgrounds, so pump trucks go where and when they are actually needed.
customer: Campground and recreation concessionaires operating on federal and state land, state park systems, county park departments, ski areas and trailhead managers. Second wave: event, construction and portable-restroom fleets. Pumping contractors are channel partners.
problem: Vault toilets are pumped on fixed calendars or when a hiker reports an overflow. Busy sites need pumping weekly or monthly in peak season and remote sites once every year or two. Trucks drive one to three hours each way. A full toilet closes a site, damages the visitor experience, and holiday weekends generate emergency call-outs at premium rates.
solution: An ultrasonic or time-of-flight sensor puck under the riser lid plus a PIR visit counter, on LTE-M with a narrowband satellite (NB-NTN) fallback for no-coverage sites. The dashboard forecasts 'days to full' from usage and holiday and weather calendars, then auto-generates work orders to the nearest contractor with route batching. Usage counts also drive restocking of toilet paper and cleaning visits.
why_now: Narrowband satellite IoT modules and plans have reached commercial availability, cutting the cost of monitoring a toilet 40 miles from cell coverage. Recreation agencies and concessionaires face tight staffing and budgets, so triaging truck rolls has real value.
revenue_model: USD 12-20 per toilet per month including a leased sensor (about USD 150 hardware cost). A 600-toilet concessionaire is about USD 100k per year. Route-optimization module for pumpers. Event-fleet pricing per unit per event.
non_obvious_insight: The savings isn't fewer pump-outs; it's knowing which toilets are near-full before a holiday weekend and avoiding closures and emergency call-outs. Pumpers earn per visit, so pitch them a route-density and demand-forecast tool that grows their business rather than threatening it.
first_30_days: Build 30 units from off-the-shelf modules. Pilot 5-10 toilets each with three concessionaires and two county park departments. Use the shoulder season (hunting and early winter trailheads) to test. Recruit one septic pumping company as a co-pilot partner. Convert to annual contracts before next spring's opening.

title: Court-Ready Estate Accounting from Bank Statements
one_liner: Upload the statements and get the court's accounting format back, so small probate firms stop losing money on the ledger.
customer: Solo and small estate and trust law firms, CPAs acting as fiduciaries, professional fiduciaries, and small trust desks at community banks.
problem: Inventories, receipts-and-disbursements accountings and trust accountings to beneficiaries take 10-30+ hours per estate. Each state and county wants a different format. Small firms bill flat fees or lose money, and errors cause objections and surcharges.
solution: Upload bank and brokerage statements (PDF or CSV). The system categorizes transactions into principal and income, ties to date-of-death balances, flags unusual disbursements, and exports state-format accountings. Start with California plus one more high-volume state (New York or Pennsylvania). A reviewer trail records every override. Later add fiduciary 1041 data and distribution schedules.
why_now: LLM document extraction only recently became reliable on messy statements. Revocable-trust use has grown with online will and trust providers, so more successor trustees face accounting duties.
revenue_model: $149-$399 per accounting or $199-$499/month per firm, with enterprise pricing for banks.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in probate isn't drafting, it's the ledger, and the ledger is what judges and beneficiaries inspect. Whoever owns the estate ledger owns the workflow and the data for tax, inventory and distributions.
first_30_days: Pick California. Recruit 10 small firms through bar section lists. Process 20 accountings manually for $199 each while capturing the county format rules. Publish a sample output for lead generation.

title: Widow's First 90 Days, Sold Through Funeral Homes
one_liner: The pharmacy sees a death first, because refills stop. Package a pharmacist-led medicine cleanup and 90-day check-in program for the surviving spouse, and sell it to funeral homes as their aftercare offering.
customer: Independent funeral homes, which pay $95-195 per family or fold it into a package. Also out-of-town adult children, who pay $29-49 a month for someone local to watch over the surviving parent. Later, Medicare Advantage plans and PACE programs.
problem: When one spouse dies, the survivor often loses the person who managed the pillbox for both. The survivor skips or double-doses their own meds. The decedent's opioids and benzodiazepines sit in the house, where they can be diverted or swallowed by a grandchild. The first months after spousal loss carry a well-documented spike in illness and mortality, yet the funeral home hands over a grief booklet and the family scatters. No institution owns the medicine cabinet.
solution: A 'Steady' kit enrolled at the arrangement conference with one text. Within a week the pharmacist collects, counts and safely disposes of the decedent's meds, using the pharmacy's DEA-authorized collector status, which funeral homes lack. The pharmacist reconciles the survivor's own meds, resets med sync with adherence packaging and delivery, and flags deprescribing candidates for the doctor. Then come structured 30/60/90-day calls covering eating, sleeping, mood, falls and missed doses, with a report to the adult child and referrals to grief support or the physician when flags trip.
why_now: The first baby boomers turn 80 in 2026, so deaths in the 75-90 cohort will climb for two decades. Small funeral homes are squeezed by cremation and consolidators and need a differentiator beyond price. Independent pharmacies need new cash services as PBM margins collapse. Startups like Empathy have shown that families, employers and insurers pay for post-death help, but none touch medicines. Opioid-settlement money is funding take-back and safe disposal.
revenue_model: Funeral home pays per enrolled family, or the fee is folded into a package uplift. Families or adult children pay a subscription for the 90-day check-in service. The pharmacy earns on med sync, delivery and adherence packaging, plus MTM comprehensive medication review fees. Later, Medicare Advantage plans and PACE programs pay for bereavement-risk outreach.
non_obvious_insight: A pharmacist learns of a death before the obituary runs, because the refill pattern stops and the survivor's profile changes. The pharmacist and the funeral director are the two professionals in every small town who deal with aging and dying. They have never shared a channel, and a disposal-authorized pharmacist is the only one who can legally take the leftover controlled drugs.
first_30_days: One pharmacy owner recruits two funeral homes in the same county. Build a one-page kit with a DEA-compliant collection procedure, a survivor med review checklist, a med-sync reset and a 30/60/90 call script. Pilot with 20 families, free to the funeral home at first, then $95 per family. Track bottles collected, discrepancies found and 90-day ER visits. Present the case study at the state funeral directors' association meeting and line up an MTM platform partner to bill the comprehensive medication reviews.

title: Pooled Tariff-Surcharge Refund Claims for Small Buyers
one_liner: Connect to small businesses' accounting data, find tariff surcharges they paid distributors, and pool their claims against the same suppliers now receiving IEEPA refunds.
customer: Restaurants and restaurant groups, contractors, small manufacturers and retailers that bought through distributors who added tariff surcharge lines in 2025, paying on contingency.
problem: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, and CBP began taking refund claims through its CAPE portal on April 20, 2026, with roughly $175B owed to about 330,000 importers. Suppliers who passed the tariff through on itemized surcharges are now collecting refunds. Small buyers who paid those lines have claims but no visibility and no lawyer, since a $3k claim is uneconomic to pursue alone.
solution: Read 24 months of AP data (QuickBooks, Bill.com, email invoices) with an LLM to isolate itemized surcharges and post-tariff price jumps by supplier. Aggregate each supplier's small-buyer claims into one pooled demand or arbitration or class action through a partner consumer-protection firm. Track which suppliers have filed for refunds. Later, add econometric analysis of 'embedded' non-itemized price increases.
why_now: Refunds are being issued now (typically 60 to 90 days after acceptance), so the window for suppliers to hold and spend the money is short. Pass-through disputes have begun to appear in courts, but law firms focus on large B2B claimants. Litigation and CBP timing remains uncertain (the government appealed the refund order), which favors moving fast.
revenue_model: 20% to 30% contingency on recovered amounts, plus a fixed fee to run the AP analysis for larger buyers.
non_obvious_insight: Claims are tiny individually but concentrated by supplier. Two hundred restaurants that all bought from the same three distributors are a multimillion-dollar claim against three defendants. The supplier-level dataset (who added surcharges, when, how much, who filed) is the moat, and it is built one small customer at a time.
first_30_days: Build a free 'surcharge finder' that scans an uploaded invoice export or QuickBooks connection and shows what was paid. Recruit through restaurant and contractor associations and bookkeepers. Sign 50 claimants on contingency and target the 10 distributors whose surcharges show up most often. Line up a partner litigation firm.

title: Rolling Bio-Uplift Trials for Frontier Labs
one_liner: A standing cohort of novices and benign-proxy wet-lab tasks that measures whether each new AI model actually helps people do biology, within weeks of release.
customer: Frontier AI lab safeguards and preparedness teams, government AI safety institutes, and operators of bio-AI verification programs; insurers later.
problem: The main large RCT (Active Site, n=153, run June-August 2025, published February 2026) found workflow completion of 5.2% with LLMs versus 6.6% with the internet. Task uplift was 1.42x and non-significant. Forecasters had predicted 27% uplift against 5% actual. By publication the tested models were about a year old. Labs now grant relaxed safeguards to verified users (Anthropic's Sept 17 program) without current evidence on which wet-lab tasks models actually change.
solution: Maintain a trained standing cohort of 100-200 novices with baselined tacit skill, in a BSL-1 lab with IRB approval done once. Use pre-approved benign-proxy tasks (plasmid construction with harmless markers, protein purification, cell culture, plaque assay with a harmless phage). Randomize model access versus internet access and return results within 2-3 weeks of each model checkpoint.
why_now: The RCT showed tacit bench skill, not knowledge, is the bottleneck, and it also exposed evaluation lag. Frontier labs ship models every few months. New verification programs make evidence on actual uplift commercially valuable to both labs and legitimate users.
revenue_model: $150-400k per model evaluation, $600k-1.5M annual retainers, and calibrated benchmark licenses to verification-program operators.
non_obvious_insight: The frontier is mostly measured with text quizzes, while risk (and benefit to legitimate labs) lives in hands-on tacit skill. Speed and cadence, not a one-off academic RCT, is the product. Active Site is a nonprofit incumbent, so expect to partner or license protocols. The cohort and lab double as a training and vetting pipeline for a bench network.
first_30_days: Contact Active Site and METR alumni for protocol and IRB templates and explore licensing rather than duplicating. Secure BSL-1 space. Recruit 40 novices and run a 3-week pilot on two open-weight models to publish methodology. Pitch 3 safeguards teams and 2 government safety bodies on a $100k pilot.

title: Insurer-Billable Circles for GLP-1 Quitters
one_liner: Twelve-week therapist-and-dietitian-led groups for people coming off GLP-1s, funded through behavioral-health and nutrition benefits rather than 'weight loss' budgets.
customer: Employers and carriers that just dropped GLP-1 coverage (about 14% more plan to by 2027) and the ex-users themselves ($299 cash cohorts to start). GLP-1 telehealth firms are a later channel, as a retention add-on.
problem: Only about a third of non-diabetic patients are still on therapy at 1 year, and cost is the top reason. Stoppers regain weight about 4x faster than behavioral losers, roughly 60% of ex-users intend to restart, and 70% report lost joy in eating. Returning food noise, binge eating and body-identity distress get no clinical owner, because pharma, PBMs and telehealth are paid for volume or price, not persistence.
solution: Small cohorts of about 8 are co-led by a licensed therapist (CBT/ACT, binge-eating experience) and a registered dietitian. Content covers returning food noise, structured eating, protein and resistance-training basics, and a relapse plan. A partner prescriber offers a taper or low-cost maintenance plan (for example a $149 pill) and defines restart triggers. Where clinically indicated (BED, adjustment disorder), sessions bill as in-network group psychotherapy (CPT 90853) with dietitian MNT, using honest coding only. Employers can instead buy it as a $450-700 per-participant 'transition benefit'.
why_now: Employer GLP-1 coverage for weight loss fell from 72% to 60% in 2026 and more employers are dropping it before open enrollment now. Brand pill prices fell to $149-$299 cash, so 'restart cheaply' is a real option. The Medicare $50 Bridge copay ends Dec 2027, and JAMA Psychiatry 2026 found GLP-1 use of about 50% among binge-eating-disorder patients.
revenue_model: In-network group-therapy and MNT claims, or an employer per-participant fee ($450-700 per 12-week cohort versus about $12k a year for the drug), plus an optional $29-49 per month prescriber maintenance subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Employers cut coverage to save money and created a pool of abrupt discontinuers with no plan. The only bundle in this space that insurers already pay for by law is behavioral-health group care, so the funding path is mental-health parity, not obesity medicine. That also aligns with the psychological cause of regain (food noise, identity, bingeing) rather than another diet.
first_30_days: Sign one therapist with binge-eating experience and one RD, both credentialed through an existing group practice. Recruit the first cohort of 8 from GLP-1 subreddits and Facebook groups at $299 cash. Approach three mid-size employers through brokers who have just announced dropped coverage. Track 12-week weight regain, binge episodes and restart rates against a naive expectation.

title: Escrow Shock Early Warning for Servicers
one_liner: Soft reinsurance produces homeowner nonrenewals, which produce force-placed cover and escrow shortages, which produce delinquencies on servicers' books. Predict and defuse the shock before it lands.
customer: Mid-size mortgage servicers (50k-1M loans), including non-bank and credit-union servicers with loss-mitigation and hazard-insurance teams.
problem: Homeowner insurance now rivals mortgage payments (Tacoma News Tribune, Aug 2026). Nonrenewals hit records (Utah highest in 2025, New Mexico a record 6,200, county rate spikes up to 33% in H1 2026). When coverage lapses or moves to a FAIR plan, escrow analyses jump payments by hundreds of dollars a month and delinquencies follow.
solution: Score every loan for escrow-shock risk 90 days out, using state nonrenewal patterns, filed rate changes, tax data and the servicer's own hazard-insurance tracking. Then run assisted outreach before the shortage letter goes out: re-shop with an agent network, mitigation credits, and payment-plan options. Deliver dashboards and borrower-level outcomes to loss-mitigation heads.
why_now: Record nonrenewals, California's FAIR Plan taking more new loans (beinsure, Aug 2026), a HELOC surge signaling stretched households, and the household credit stress in the brief (record auto delinquencies, K-shaped economy).
revenue_model: $75-$200 per borrower resolved, or $0.50-$1.00 per loan per year SaaS. Optional share of avoided force-placed premium.
non_obvious_insight: Servicers treat insurance as lapse-tracking compliance, not delinquency prevention. A single loss-mitigation case can cost hundreds of dollars, so even a 1% reduction in shock-driven delinquency pays for the product. Target servicers with investor and regulator pressure, since some earn money on force-placed cover.
first_30_days: Build a free escrow-shock heat map for three states from public data as a lead magnet. Cold-outreach loss-mitigation heads at 30 mid-size and credit-union servicers, and sign one pilot on about 20k loans.

title: Savings Groups Finance Apprenticeships via Income-Share
one_liner: A mobile-money tool that lets a village savings group use its year-end share-out to pay a workshop for a young member's apprenticeship and starter toolkit, then collect 10-12% of that apprentice's income for two years back into the group.
customer: Village savings and loan groups, chamas and small SACCOs of 20-30 members in Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, which pay the fees. Workshops and TVET trainers who get paid upfront, and employers such as solar installers who want certified graduates, pay referral and placement fees.
problem: Formal training plus tools costs $150-500, which is out of reach for a household living on irregular farm income. Youth have no credit history. Income-share agreements have mostly failed in rich countries because income verification and collection cost more than the loan. Meanwhile savings groups hold a pile of cash at each year-end share-out and have few productive places to put it.
solution: A USSD and WhatsApp workflow. The group votes on a candidate. The group pays the trainer in tranches confirmed by attendance and milestone photos. The tool collects a set share of the graduate's mobile-money income into the group ledger, and members receive returns pro rata. Social collateral does the enforcement, so no bureau or aggregator is needed. Legally it is structured as an income-linked group loan, not a security.
why_now: Sandi AI reports 10,000+ farmer groups across Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania pooling savings for solar irrigation instead of borrowing, so groups will invest pooled money in productive assets. Africa's solar and battery installs are growing about 45% a year and 75% of that is distributed, which creates paid technician work. With six seed rounds for every Series A, outside capital is scarce and group capital is the reachable pool. Reported pressure on Gulf remittances, about $50bn at risk, weakens family-funded schooling.
revenue_model: A 4% origination fee on training payments, 1% of repayments, and 5-8% referral fees from trainers and tool vendors. Placement fees of about $20 per graduate come from installers and employers. Youth-employment funders can pay $100-200 per verified income outcome, which is what makes the thin margin work at small scale.
non_obvious_insight: The income-share agreement broke in rich countries on enforcement, and a savings group solves enforcement at zero marginal cost because members know the apprentice, the workshop and the family. The year-end share-out also lands in December, right before January apprenticeship intake, so a timing mismatch becomes a built-in cash cycle.
first_30_days: Partner with a savings-group promoter NGO or a platform like Sandi AI. Choose five groups within three months of their share-out. Sign three workshops (welding, solar installation, motorcycle repair or tailoring) to milestone-based payment. Launch 10 apprenticeships worth $3-4k, funded by the groups' own money plus a small first-loss guarantee from a grant. Track progress by photo and voice notes on WhatsApp, and record the first income repayments.

title: Independent Collateral Audits for GPU-Backed Loans
one_liner: A floorplan-audit business for private credit: physically verify, monitor and value the GPUs that secure a fast-growing pile of debt.
customer: Mid-market private credit funds, family-office lenders, equipment-finance arms and ABS trustees with GPU-backed facilities. Neocloud borrowers are a second payer, since verified collateral lowers their cost of capital.
problem: Over $20 billion of GPU-backed debt existed by early 2026, typically advancing 50-70% of appraised value, yet the resale value depends on obsolescence assumptions that are unsettled. Two large neoclouds use depreciation schedules of six and four years on similar hardware. Lenders mostly rely on borrower-provided reports and cannot see the rack, so they cannot confirm that serial numbers exist, are powered, are utilized and are located where the collateral schedule says.
solution: Borrow the car-dealer floorplan audit playbook. Field technicians verify serial numbers via BMC/IPMI readouts and photos, check rack location and power draw, sample cluster utilization through read-only telemetry attestations, review hosting contracts, insurance and cooling health, and grade condition. Deliver a quarterly report to the lender, then build continuous monitoring and a published GPU residual-value index.
why_now: GPU-backed credit scaled from experiment to institutional product in 2025-26. The next-generation architecture transition in 2026 and the rolling-off of 2023-24 contracts make collateral quality the central credit question, and lenders new to the asset class have no in-house inspectors.
revenue_model: $5-25k per site audit and $2-8k per month for monitoring, paid by lenders and sometimes borrowers. Later, data license revenue from the residual-value index.
non_obvious_insight: A GPU loan looks like equipment finance but behaves like tech inventory concentrated in a few sites. The missing service is not analytics but a trusted human in the room. Aircraft and auto-floorplan lenders solved this decades ago, and a small team of ex-data-center technicians plus one equipment-finance lawyer can do the same.
first_30_days: Team up two ex-data-center technicians with an equipment-finance lawyer. Approach 10 mid-market lenders and GPU-lease brokers. Offer one first audit at cost for a lender-borrower pair. Standardize the deliverable (serial check, photos, power and uptime, contract review) and publish an anonymized sample report to win the next five audits.

title: Blinded Diligence Bureau for AI-Biotech Financiers
one_liner: A buyer-paid, blinded prospective testing service that tells pharma BD teams, royalty funds and lenders whether an AI drug-discovery platform's claims hold up in a neutral wet lab.
customer: Pharma BD&L and search-and-evaluation teams, corporate VCs, venture lenders, synthetic-royalty funds and crossover investors underwriting AI biotechs.
problem: AI-biotech capital is enormous ($6B+ in 2026, including Isomorphic's $2.1B and Chai's $400M). Deals are headlined in biobucks: Genentech-Earendil is $55M upfront against $1.5B+ total. Buyers still rely on vendor-supplied retrospective slides. The public competitions (Adaptyv, Anthropic x Adaptyv) test protein binding only and are public, not confidential diligence on a buyer's own targets. Small-molecule, antibody and ADMET claims have no neutral test.
solution: A custom blinded bake-off. The buyer picks 5-20 targets or properties (binding, potency, developability, ADMET). Two to four shortlisted vendors submit designs under NDA. Neutral partner labs assay them blind: an Adaptyv-style lab for binders, a CRO for ADMET. The buyer gets a ranked result, hit rate versus controls, a free open-model baseline (Boltz, BindCraft and similar) and a red-flag memo. Vendors never pay for ranking.
why_now: Frontier-lab designs hit about 27% in Adaptyv's blind test (1,320 designs, 16 targets, 354 binders), so 'does it beat free open models' is now the right question. Software-only AI shops are wobbling (Schrodinger cut staff), and mega-rounds attract generalist money that cannot judge the science. At least 12 funded biotechs sold for $1B+ this year, so acquirers need fast technical diligence. Adaptyv just raised $40M, so neutral wet-lab capacity can be rented.
revenue_model: $60-250k per blinded engagement, $150k/year retainers for funds that see 10+ platforms, and anonymized aggregate 'state of AI design' reports as a secondary product.
non_obvious_insight: 'Beats a free open-source baseline' is the question nobody prices. Buyer-paid independence, with no vendor fees, is the only credible model. Neutral labs already exist to rent, and consultancies lack lab access. Competitions such as Adaptyv's are partners and lead sources, not rivals, because they are public and binder-only.
first_30_days: Pitch 5 corporate-VC and BD teams currently evaluating platforms and sign 2 pilots at $40-60k. Rent capacity from an Adaptyv-style lab and one CRO. Design a 10-target panel with 3 anonymized vendors plus an open-model baseline. Publish the methodology to build trust.

title: Insured Filing Clerk for Multi-City Contractor Licenses
one_liner: A computer-use agent that renews and files contractor and business licenses across city and county portals that have no APIs, backed by a penalty warranty.
customer: Trade contractors (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, roofers, landscapers, painters), mobile groomers, food trucks and short-term-rental hosts working across many cities or counties, with 2-30 employees.
problem: Each city and county has its own business-license, registration and permit portal, fee schedule and renewal date, with COI and bond uploads. Missing one triggers fines or stop-work orders. Enterprise-priced compliance vendors ignore small firms, and payroll vendors are bundling only payroll compliance (Gusto bought Mosey in April 2026).
solution: An agent operates the same portals a human would to renew, upload COIs and bonds, pay fees with a virtual card and capture receipts. Human reviewers verify sensitive steps. A warranty pays penalties for missed or incorrect filings. Every filing improves a jurisdiction knowledge base of forms, fees and quirks.
why_now: Browser and computer-use agents crossed a reliability threshold in 2025-26, and payroll compliance has been productized, leaving licenses and permits as the untouched adjacent layer.
revenue_model: $59/month plus $15 per filing plus fee pass-through, with the warranty cost built into pricing.
non_obvious_insight: With roughly 19,000 municipalities, no API strategy will ever cover the map, but an agent that uses the human interface can. The moat is the jurisdiction graph and the warranty.
first_30_days: Pick a dense metro cluster with many cities and one trade. Assist 20 contractors with renewals, recording each portal flow, and sign a COI and bond partner for bulk uploads. Track error rate and hours saved.

title: PO-Backed Working Capital for Drone Sub-Tier
one_liner: A specialty lender that advances cash against Gauntlet-winner purchase orders to the motor, battery and casting shops that must ship first.
customer: Sub-tier suppliers (motors, ESCs, battery packs, castings, machined parts) with 10-200 staff feeding Drone Dominance winners and Navy autonomy programs; funded by a debt fund or family office.
problem: Insiders think mega-rounds fix the defense supply chain. The AIA-Bain study says no fit-for-purpose investment model exists for sub-tier makers. About 60,000 drones are being ordered, but the people who make the parts are too small for VC and too risky for banks.
solution: Underwrite the prime's award notice and delivery schedule, not the supplier's balance sheet. Offer PO advances, tooling leases and milestone-linked draws, with payment routed through the prime so the loan is self-liquidating. Public award data plus supplier-network mapping is the underwriting edge.
why_now: Gauntlet 2 (Sept 2026) produced roughly 60,000 units of orders. The Navy is stepping back to Series D-F co-investment. $14.6B of 2026 VC is going to primes, not the parts makers beneath them.
revenue_model: 1.5-3% per month on advances (10-15% blended yield), plus origination fees, plus small equity warrants on the best suppliers.
non_obvious_insight: The constraint is not capital in general but capital shaped like a receivable from a credit-worthy prime. Whoever routes payment through the prime turns a scary startup-supplier loan into near-prime credit.
first_30_days: Sign one debt-fund partner for a $5M pilot line. Pull award notices for the 19 Gauntlet 2 firms and cold-call their top 5 suppliers each. Fund 3 small POs against prime payment-assignment letters.

title: Verified-MW Truth Feed for Data Center Load
one_liner: A probability score and satellite-plus-permit verification of every large-load request, so planners and investors can tell the real 42 GW from the 201 GW of paper.
customer: Utility load-forecast and IRP teams, ISOs, state PUC staff and consumer advocates. Hedge funds, infrastructure investors and equipment makers buy the same feed as alternative data.
problem: About 36.6 GW is under construction versus about 201 GW 'in planning'. Developers file duplicate requests at several utilities, utilities over-forecast, and ratepayers fund the generation and wires built for load that never shows up. Even xAI's Memphis battery is '2.8 GWh counted versus 3.3 GWh claimed' and nobody verifies it.
solution: Fuse interconnection filings, zoning and permit records, tax abatements, transformer and switchgear procurement signals, construction imagery (SAR and optical), thermal signatures of cooling plants and tariff deposits into a per-project probability of energization by date and MW online. Ship it as an API, quarterly reports and exhibits usable in regulatory proceedings.
why_now: Large-load requests are exploding, utilities are adding deposit rules, and cheap satellite data plus LLM document parsing lets a three-person team do this.
revenue_model: $30-500k a year per investor subscription and $75-300k per utility or ISO, with discounted licenses for consumer advocates.
non_obvious_insight: The most expensive number in the grid is the load forecast, and it is built from self-reported requests. Hedge funds already want the same data for AI-capex tracking, so they can fund a public-interest product.
first_30_days: Build datasets for Virginia, Ohio and Texas. Publish a 'phantom load index'. Sell three alternative-data subscriptions at $30-50k. Offer free trials to two consumer advocate offices.

title: Operator-of-Record for Enterprise Drone Flights
one_liner: A licensed BVLOS operations team-as-a-service that files the waivers, runs the safety case and supervises the flights for utilities, solar developers and pipeline owners.
customer: Mid-size utilities and co-ops, solar and wind developers, pipeline and rail operators, ports, mines, and their insurers.
problem: BVLOS technology is ready, but organizations lack the capability: waiver applications, safety cases, ops manuals, remote-pilot staffing and data pipelines. The final status of Part 108 (the FAA BVLOS rule) could not be verified, which adds uncertainty. Meanwhile the DJI ban forces fleet refreshes.
solution: A reusable safety-case library and remote-pilot center (one pilot supervising 5-10 drone docks) running US-made drone-in-a-box fleets. Price per line-mile or per site, with data delivered into the customer's GIS and maintenance systems.
why_now: The December 2025 DJI restrictions force fleet replacement decisions in 2026, and Wing's 1M deliveries show BVLOS operations working at scale. Whatever Part 108's final form, operators still need documented safety cases and waivers.
revenue_model: $5-20k per month per site retainer or per-line-mile pricing on multi-year MSAs, plus waiver and safety-case consulting fees.
non_obvious_insight: Regulation is a one-time cost that vendors avoid, but the operator-of-record that accumulates waivers, flight logs and accepted safety cases builds a moat that compounds with every approval.
first_30_days: Pick one region (for example co-ops in Texas or Colorado) and partner with one US-made dock vendor. Get one co-op to sign a pilot covering 20 substations, file the waiver, and aim for the first inspection within 60 days.

title: Tariff Refund Liquidation-Cliff Radar
one_liner: A deadline tracker and filing generator for small importers and small customs brokers that tells them, entry by entry, which refund route is still open and when it closes.
customer: Importers with 200-20,000 entries per year, and independent customs brokers serving them, who lack in-house trade counsel. Priced per entry or as a success fee.
problem: CBP will not refund automatically. Filers must act through CAPE, a Post Summary Correction (PSC) or a protest, and each route has a different window. CAPE Phase 1 accepts only unliquidated entries or entries liquidated in the preceding 80 days. Protests must be filed within 180 days of liquidation. PSCs must be filed within 300 days of entry or 15 days before liquidation. Finally liquidated entries, drawback, TIB and reconciliation entries are ineligible. The importer also needs ACE Portal access and ACH enrollment on file. Any outstanding CBP debt is offset first under 19 CFR 24.72.
solution: The tool ingests the ACE entry summary and liquidation reports (ES-003 or ES-022 exports, or a broker CSV). It assigns every IEEPA-duty entry a status and route (CAPE-eligible now, protest-only, PSC window, ineligible) and a hard 'last day' date. It auto-builds CAPE declaration files (up to 9,999 entries) for the broker and protest packets for the rest. It reconciles ACH deposits and interest against the ACE refund reports (REV-603 and REV-615) so the finance team can book the refund entry by entry. It flags CBP-debt offsets and scam solicitations, since CBP has warned about fraudsters targeting refund claimants.
why_now: The rolling cliff is live. Every month another vintage of 2025 entries liquidates, and each has a fresh 80-day CAPE window and a 180-day protest window that can lapse silently. Refunds are being recognised in one lump. AutoZone's alone was worth $4.43 EPS in a quarter. Auditors will require entry-level tie-outs.
revenue_model: $3-8 per entry tracked, $25K-$75K annual site licences for small brokers with 50+ importer clients, or a 3-5% success fee on refunds recovered from entries that would otherwise have gone finally liquidated.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is a calendar, not law-firm expertise. CBP's own pages say 'ACE accepts CAPE Declarations containing entries liquidated within the preceding 80 days', 'once an entry has liquidated, a protest may be filed within 180 days', and 'you cannot remove entries from the Declaration' once filed (https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/trade-remedies/ieepa-duty-refunds and https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/trade-remedies/IEEPA-FAQ). CBP says only the IOR or its broker can file, and the FAQ never mentions automatic refunds. Public companies are already booking eight-figure refunds (AutoZone about $96M, MillerKnoll $16.5M, Worthington $4M: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/23/worthington-wor-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). The long tail of small importers is running on broker email chains and is the most likely to lose entries to a missed window.
first_30_days: Cold-email and call 100 independent customs brokers (from NCBFAA and local port broker lists) with an offer: 'send us your entry list and we'll return a route-and-deadline sheet within 24 hours, free'. Build the classifier in a spreadsheet plus a Python script. Publish a public liquidation-date calculator as a lead magnet aimed at importers. Convert the first 3 brokers to a paid per-entry contract, and have each refer 5-10 importer clients.
